findings.title: Scheduled sends cancellation uses sendgrid batch cancel without checking previous cancel limit, no error handling for individual failures
findings.body: The cron now cancels reminders marked 'cancelled' within the next hour via SendGrid's scheduled_sends cancel API, then deletes the DB record. If the SendGrid request throws (e.g. due to the same 100-pending-cancellation limit mentioned in the PR description, or any transient API error), the entire loop's try/catch wraps all iterations, so a single failure aborts the whole batch (workflowRemindersToDelete never gets Promise.all'd for remaining items, and already-cancelled-in-SendGrid items that failed DB delete won't retry correctly). This can still result in silently stuck 'cancelled' reminders whose emails are sent anyway if they fall outside the next cron run's time window overlap assumptions, or lead to duplicate cancel calls on subsequent runs that may error out and block the rest of the batch again.

findings.title: immediateDelete bypasses cancellation-limit issue the PR intends to fix
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder still supports an 'immediateDelete' path (used in handleNewBooking.ts reschedule flow and workflows.tsx step-delete flow) that directly calls the SendGrid cancel endpoint synchronously, which is exactly the behavior that caused the original bug (exceeding the 100 pending cancellations limit documented in the PR description). Since this path is still used for immediate deletes (e.g., on reschedule of previous booking, step deletion, workflow deletion), those cases are not protected by the new 'cancelled' flag + cron batching mechanism, and could still experience the same silent failure once more than 100 cancellations are pending at once.

findings.title: Removed deleteMany of to-be-removed reminders when event types deactivated
findings.body: Previously the code also called ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany for reminders being removed when event types are deactivated. The new code only calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder (which, for EMAIL, now just sets the 'cancelled' flag rather than deleting), but never deletes the row from the DB in this update() flow for the 'removedEventTypes' case. Since these reminders are tied to bookings that remain in the activeOn relation state after this update, this may leave orphaned WorkflowReminder rows that are only cleaned up by the cron if 'scheduledDate' is within the next hour — otherwise they persist indefinitely, and if the event type is later reactivated, the booking may not get a new reminder since the old row still exists with cancelled=true, scheduled=true referencing an old obsolete batch, blocking the new unscheduled-reminder path from re-creating one for that booking given no uniqueness check here on bookingUid/workflowStepId pair but risk of leftover stale cancelled reminders never purged in time to free email sends is still present.

findings.title: SMS reminder deletion remains synchronous but no cancelled-flag batching like email
findings.body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the WorkflowReminder row immediately after calling twilio.cancelSMS, unlike the new two-phase (cancelled flag + cron deletion) approach for email. If twilio.cancelSMS throws for some reason (e.g., rate limiting or already-passed cancellation window), the whole function throws before prisma.workflowReminder.delete runs, by design in the try/catch it's swallowed, but the reminder row then still exists in a scheduled state and will still attempt to send via Twilio since nothing marks it cancelled; there's no retry or cron-based cleanup path for SMS now, meaning the original cancellation reliability issue described in the PR for emails is not fully addressed for SMS reminders.
